authority: PD 851 and its Revised Guidelines (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.13 §§A–D, F): a twelfth of the basic salary earned in the calendar year, rank-and-file only. §B.4: not owed to those paid on purely commission, boundary or task basis or a fixed amount for specific work (`TASK_BASIS`), except piece-rate workers (`PIECE_RATE`), who are covered (§F.1). Separation pay
authority: Labor Code art.298: one month’s pay or one month per year of service, whichever is higher, on termination for installation of labour-saving devices or redundancy; art.298–299: half a month per year or one month, whichever is higher, on retrenchment, closure not due to serious losses, or disease. A fraction of at least six months counts as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Labor Code arts.298–299: one month’s pay per year of service (redundancy, the only authorised cause the exit reasons distinguish; a fraction of at least six months counts as a year), never less than one month. Tax: exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b) as pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control (redundancy or retrenchment), so the class counts toward nothing and no withholding scheme reads it. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the exit fact `termination_cause` chooses the award — labour-saving devices or redundancy one month a year (art.298); retrenchment, a closure not due to serious losses, or disease half a month a year (arts.298–299); a closure due to serious business losses owes none (art.298: the half-month award is for closures "not due to serious business losses"). Applied in place 2026-09-29 in every version (ML-3, a transcription omission): a termination for disease recorded as a dismissal or unilateral termination of a non-domestic employee (exit fact `terminated_for_disease`) pays the same one month or half a month per year, whichever is greater (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323: "at least to one (1) month salary or to one-half (1/2) month salary for every year of service, whichever is greater"); tax-exempt as separation for sickness (NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b)). A kasambahay's disease is a just cause under RA 10361 s.34(f) with no separation pay.

name: Protection-order support (RA 9262)
authority: RA 9262 s.8(g) (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/22128): a protection order may direct the respondent to provide support, and notwithstanding other laws to the contrary the court orders an appropriate percentage of the respondent's income or salary withheld regularly by the employer and automatically remitted directly to the woman; failure to withhold or remit, or delay without justifiable cause, makes the employer liable for indirect contempt. Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (ML-2, a transcription omission: RA 9262 predates every version). The percentage is the court's, so the employer deducts exactly the amount the served order fixes for the period, entered by HR with the order as evidence. Owner rule 2026-09-28: the Act is silent on how the employer books the withholding; default a net-pay deduction after every statutory line, touching no SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG or withholding base, because the support is paid out of the respondent's own compensation. Remittance to the payee is an external payment (obligation PROTECTION_ORDER_SUPPORT_WITHHOLDING).

name: Retirement pay
authority: RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): an employee retiring at 60 to 65 after at least five years’ service, with no retirement plan, is paid half a month’s salary for every year of service — 22.5 days: fifteen days, the five-day service incentive leave and one twelfth of the 13th-month pay — a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): optional retirement from sixty and compulsory at sixty-five, after five years’ service — a person retiring past sixty-five is inside it; retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten workers are outside (`company.facts.small_establishment`). One-half month salary is 22.5 days of the daily rate, the daily rate being the monthly basic on the person’s own factor (365 for the monthly-paid, 313 on a six-day week, 261 on five). authority: Labor Code art.298: one month’s pay or one month per year of service, whichever is higher, on termination for installation of labour-saving devices or redundancy; art.298–299: half a month per year or one month, whichever is higher, on retrenchment, closure not due to serious losses, or disease. name: Retirement pay
authority: RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): an employee retiring at 60 to 65 after at least five years’ service, with no retirement plan, is paid half a month’s salary for every year of service — 22.5 days: fifteen days, the five-day service incentive leave and one twelfth of the 13th-month pay — a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): optional retirement from sixty and compulsory at sixty-five, after five years’ service — a person retiring past sixty-five is inside it; retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten workers are outside (`company.facts.small_establishment`). One-half month salary is 22.5 days of the daily rate, the daily rate being the monthly basic on the person’s own factor (365 for the monthly-paid, 313 on a six-day week, 261 on five). authority: Labor Code art.298: one month’s pay or one month per year of service, whichever is higher, on termination for installation of labour-saving devices or redundancy; art.298–299: half a month per year or one month, whichever is higher, on retrenchment, closure not due to serious losses, or disease. A fraction of at least six months counts as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Labor Code arts.298–299: one month’s pay per year of service (redundancy, the only authorised cause the exit reasons distinguish; a fraction of at least six months counts as a year), never less than one month. Tax: exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b) as pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control (redundancy or retrenchment), so the class counts toward nothing and no withholding scheme reads it. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the exit fact `termination_cause` chooses the award — labour-saving devices or redundancy one month a year (art.298); retrenchment, a closure not due to serious losses, or disease half a month a year (arts.298–299); a closure due to serious business losses owes none (art.298: the half-month award is for closures "not due to serious business losses"). Applied in place 2026-09-29 in every version (ML-3, a transcription omission): a termination for disease recorded as a dismissal or unilateral termination of a non-domestic employee (exit fact `terminated_for_disease`) pays the same one month or half a month per year, whichever is greater (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323: "at least to one (1) month salary or to one-half (1/2) month salary for every year of service, whichever is greater"); tax-exempt as separation for sickness (NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b)). Separation pay
authority: Labor Code art.298: one month’s pay or one month per year of service, whichever is higher, on termination for installation of labour-saving devices or redundancy; art.298–299: half a month per year or one month, whichever is higher, on retrenchment, closure not due to serious losses, or disease. A fraction of at least six months counts as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Labor Code arts.298–299: one month’s pay per year of service (redundancy, the only authorised cause the exit reasons distinguish; a fraction of at least six months counts as a year), never less than one month. Tax: exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b) as pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control (redundancy or retrenchment), so the class counts toward nothing and no withholding scheme reads it. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the exit fact `termination_cause` chooses the award — labour-saving devices or redundancy one month a year (art.298); retrenchment, a closure not due to serious losses, or disease half a month a year (arts.298–299); a closure due to serious business losses owes none (art.298: the half-month award is for closures "not due to serious business losses"). Applied in place 2026-09-29 in every version (ML-3, a transcription omission): a termination for disease recorded as a dismissal or unilateral termination of a non-domestic employee (exit fact `terminated_for_disease`) pays the same one month or half a month per year, whichever is greater (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323: "at least to one (1) month salary or to one-half (1/2) month salary for every year of service, whichever is greater"); tax-exempt as separation for sickness (NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b)). A kasambahay's disease is a just cause under RA 10361 s.34(f) with no separation pay.

name: Protection-order support (RA 9262)
authority: RA 9262 s.8(g) (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/22128): a protection order may direct the respondent to provide support, and notwithstanding other laws to the contrary the court orders an appropriate percentage of the respondent's income or salary withheld regularly by the employer and automatically remitted directly to the woman; failure to withhold or remit, or delay without justifiable cause, makes the employer liable for indirect contempt. Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (ML-2, a transcription omission: RA 9262 predates every version). The percentage is the court's, so the employer deducts exactly the amount the served order fixes for the period, entered by HR with the order as evidence. Owner rule 2026-09-28: the Act is silent on how the employer books the withholding; default a net-pay deduction after every statutory line, touching no SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG or withholding base, because the support is paid out of the respondent's own compensation. Remittance to the payee is an external payment (obligation PROTECTION_ORDER_SUPPORT_WITHHOLDING).

name: Retirement pay
authority: RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): an employee retiring at 60 to 65 after at least five years’ service, with no retirement plan, is paid half a month’s salary for every year of service — 22.5 days: fifteen days, the five-day service incentive leave and one twelfth of the 13th-month pay — a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): optional retirement from sixty and compulsory at sixty-five, after five years’ service — a person retiring past sixty-five is inside it; retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten workers are outside (`company.facts.small_establishment`). One-half month salary is 22.5 days of the daily rate, the daily rate being the monthly basic on the person’s own factor (365 for the monthly-paid, 313 on a six-day week, 261 on five). Tax: the statutory benefit is exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a), which is why this class pays the RA 7641 minimum only — any excess over it under a company plan would be tested against RA 4917 (age 50, ten years’ service, BIR-qualified plan). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): the exemption is its own required entity fact, `company.facts.retirement_exempt_establishment` — RA 7641 exempts retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten employees, a different class from the SIL exemption of any establishment regularly employing fewer than ten (`small_establishment`); a small manufacturer owes retirement pay.

Kasambahay unjustified-departure salary forfeiture
authority: RA 10361 s.32 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514): a domestic worker who leaves without justifiable reason forfeits unpaid salary of no more than fifteen days. This NET deduction is capped by the final payslip’s unpaid salary; the thirteenth-month pay and leave conversion are not salary for this cap.

name: Kasambahay unjust-dismissal indemnity
authority: RA 10361 s.32: "If the domestic worker is unjustly dismissed, the domestic worker shall be paid the compensation already earned plus the equivalent of fifteen (15) days work by way of indemnity" (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514). The Act is silent on the day: fifteen of the version’s ordinary days (`terms.ordinary_day`, the monthly basic over `ordinary_divisor_days`), the day every other PH day-rate reads. Tax: a separation for a cause beyond the employee’s control, NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b), so the class counts toward nothing, like SEPARATION_PAY. The pay-request person context evaluates the version’s ordinary divisor and roster week on the event date.
